findings.title: Refresh the dataset edge before enforcing the gate
findings.description: `status` reads the stored `tick_dataset_edge`; it does not query Databento. That edge is refreshed by `AvailabilityPhase` during a tick pass. Both cutover modes run this gate before reaching their estimate/pass, and tick has no timer. Consequently, an edge last observed during November keeps rejecting the December cutover even after the provider publishes the required data; rerunning cannot unblock it. Obtain a fresh edge through a free provider call before comparing it, and test the stale-cache case.

findings.title: Include the tick tier in per-family exit checks
findings.description:
`coverage_reads()` visits only `entry.history`, omitting both products’ configured `tbbo` tiers. `_family_evidence()` therefore never applies the not-caught-up exit rule or ledger/raw comparison to those families, although accounting includes them.

For example, a verified TBBO unit without a failure reason is accepted by `_unit_is_final()` as awaiting definitions, while its session is `awaiting_ingest`—a bucket the new exit rule explicitly rejects. With unchanged health and a zero second estimate, this omission allows an incorrect PASS. Include each configured tier over its wanted range and add a regression test.

findings.title: Preserve the family when naming cross-tier failures
findings.description: Statistics coverage includes volume verdicts for multiple families, but `over_sessions()` discards each verdict’s `family`, and the caller groups names only by product. `over_failures()` consequently attaches the same combined session list to every failing family. A TBBO-only volume discrepancy can be reported as an OHLCV discrepancy, including the wrong traded count. Preserve and match `(product, family)` when collecting and reporting these names; test differing verdicts for the same session across families.
